short: Serving a consistent, measured quantity every single time.
seoTitle: Portion Control — Meaning and Example for Businesses
metaDescription: Serving a consistent, measured quantity every single time. Portioning is where costed recipes meet reality. Part of the free Setu business glossary.
definition: Portion control is the practice of serving a consistent measured quantity of each item every time, using scales, scoops, ladles and standardised containers rather than judgement.
bodyHtml:
Why Portion Control matters

Portioning is where costed recipes meet reality. A gravy ladled ten percent heavy on every plate turns a 30% food cost into 33% without anything else changing, and nobody notices until the month closes.

How Portion Control works in practice

Standardise the serving tools per dish, weigh a sample of plates during service, and retrain when portions drift. Consistency also protects the guest experience, since customers notice a smaller plate faster than they notice a price rise.

Worked example

A 20 g overpour of a ₹400/kg sauce on 120 plates a day costs about ₹28,800 a year.

faq.question: How do I check portioning without slowing service?
faq.answer: Spot-weigh a few plates at random during a shift rather than auditing everything.

faq.question: Is portion control the same as shrinking portions?
faq.answer: No. It means serving the costed portion accurately; reducing the costed portion is a separate pricing decision.
